| | | | | | Friend,
Today, former Las Cruces Mayor Ken Miyagishima announced that he is ending his campaign for Governor and joining ours.
In announcing his endorsement, Ken shared:
_**“I realized that the best way to make a difference in New Mexico is by teaming up with my good friend, and former Mayor Gregg Hull.”**_
Ken and I did not enter this race from the same political party. We served different cities in different parts of our state. Yet as mayors, we faced many of the same challenges, and we learned that potholes are not Republican or Democratic, public safety is not a partisan issue, and creating good jobs should never take a back seat to political games.
We both know what it means to lead a city, balance a budget, work with people from every background, and be held accountable for real results.
That is why Ken’s endorsement matters.
This campaign is becoming a place where New Mexicans can come together around something bigger than party labels: safer communities, a stronger economy, better schools, responsible leadership, and a state government that works for the people it serves.
Ken could have stepped away from this race quietly. Instead, he chose to stand with us and help build the coalition needed to win in November.
**Now I am asking you to stand with us too.**
Our opponent will have millions of dollars and a national fundraising network behind her. We are building something different: a New Mexico campaign powered by people ready to move our state in a new direction.
**Will you contribute $25, $50, $100, or another amount today to help us share this endorsement across New Mexico and reach the voters who will decide this election?**
---

| | This is more than one endorsement. It is proof that New Mexicans are ready to move beyond the same old divisions and choose leadership grounded in experience, cooperation, and results.
Ken and I are joining forces. With your help, we will bring New Mexico together and win.
Thank you,

This is my opponent Scott Desjarlais. Just a month ago, after unspeakable damage to our communities, he **celebrated** funding ICE... and insisted it's for the safety of Americans.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4659ce35-4bba-428a-a3f0-3871c8de2df7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But let's be clear here, George Washington was a British subject born in colonial America. Alexander Hamilton was born in the Caribbean. Thomas Paine came from England. James Wilson came from Scotland. Long before the United States even existed, the people who shaped it were people who crossed oceans, built new lives, and helped define what this country would become.
**In other words, the word** _**immigrant**_**has been part of the American story since the very beginning, and funding breaking down that community isn 't some fix-all.**
**[I'm fighting for leadership that focuses on people, not division, and would be honored to have your help today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN TO HOMETOWNS OVER HEADLINES!!️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lately, though, you'd think the word "immigrant" itself was some kind of insult. It isn't. An immigrant is simply someone who comes to a new country. Throughout American history those people have built farms, cities, railroads, schools, businesses, and communities. They've served in our military, cared for our neighbors, started companies, and raised families that are just as American as anyone else.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fcca5395-7dd6-4bcb-abe4-4be47b06684a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### The word immigrant isn't a cuss word. It's part of the American story.
When politicians reduce complicated history to a single soundbite, it shrinks the conversation instead of expanding it. America wasn't built by one group of people or one generation. It was built by pioneers, workers, farmers, builders, dreamers, and yes, immigrants too. That has always been the reality of this country, whether some people want to admit it or not.
I'm not running to inflame debates or score viral moments online. This campaign exists because communities need leaders who actually show up, listen, and focus on the real challenges families are facing every day. Keeping our families safe, supporting struggling small businesses, helping families trying to get ahead, and aid parents working to give their kids better opportunities than they had.
If you want leadership focused on communities instead of outrage, help us keep moving forward. **[Even a small contribution helps us keep spreading a message grounded in reality and respect for the people who make this country work.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE $15 !](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a77dc7f0-b3d2-435f-8b68-1d86f463cd7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Because at the end of the day, America's strength has never come from dividing people into categories. It has come from people showing up, working hard, and building something bigger together. **That 's the future I'm fighting for.**

Back in 2003, when I was still in med school and flared jeans were all the rage, South Carolina *actually* had a Democratic Senator.

And that’s what we’re aiming for again in 2026 – a Democratic Senator to fight for all of you. **But let me be clear: our campaign just entered a brand-new, uncharted phase.**

While we don’t know our opponent yet, what we do know is whoever they are, they're starting at $0, which means Republicans are chomping at the bit to pour as much money as possible into keeping this seat red.

That’s why when I tell you we haven’t faced a more critical moment in this entire campaign, I mean it.

body:
| | | | | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0010FJT4VWAsVihqg1j-t_Gb9QtIAgb3UNGxl8j7U80S7yGBkiS4qIm0gmNo74OZ6almguANLL4E4WwZJyOZk_cfPdQpZDY6gmdLwUudGn5iQdzQLZj_2WhcY-JqtMf4iGeRedbj97-d_TdQSrnKReKHbbxlI5AIWsjjml-bEJbbbWBzNfzMbS_sR9FwrOxONi1PFK3j-znW58MhPTgcUUNPMDIgxQFmroB_tsREsw2zEp9g7o_OI6pwg==&c=hhEYYuOo6oYCrDRnaEhbiLGXdwWFOeRTbU7gDvhKWHBSfUwRvUI-Pw==&ch=9wWSqIxftMqmsjrOiqKjJBCCzpFbpbrAOCkezoy5ytPb9Q26e3ZSCQ==)

| Peter,
This week, we called on our own nominee for the U.S. Senate to withdraw. We hold every candidate who seeks to carry our banner to the highest standard, and we stand with women and survivors. That principle does not bend based on party affiliation.
He has now withdrawn.
The hard decision in this story was not ours. It belonged to the women who came forward, because speaking up is often costly, and we respect them for it.
Our responsibility required judgment and a willingness to act when circumstances demanded it. Circumstances demanded it. We acted.
Now we want to talk to you about what happens next, because it matters enormously.
There is no Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in Maine.
Our party will come together, as our rules provide, to choose the Democrat who will carry our banner against Susan Collins. We will do it carefully and we will do it right. Mainers deserve nothing less.
But here is the hard truth about that gap:
Susan Collins does not pause while we confer. She has been raising money for this race for six years. Her campaign is raising more today, and it will raise more tomorrow. The corporate PACs and wealthy interests her votes protect are not waiting to see who our nominee is. They are adding to a war chest six years in the making, while our side has no candidate, no campaign, and no one answering. Whoever we choose will start this race six years behind.
Every day of this holding period is a day she banks money unanswered.
We refuse to let our next nominee start from zero.
So the Maine Democratic Party is opening the Day One Fund: money raised now, held ready, so that the moment our new nominee is chosen, they inherit a running start instead of an empty account.
Day one, they will need a statewide organizing operation already paid for.
Day one, they will need voter contact already underway in all 16 counties.
Day one, they will need to answer Collins on the air, not spend a month catching up.
[That is what this fund does. Not a bailout, not a rainy-day account. A running start, waiting for whoever earns the nomination. Can you help power us with a split contribution between Maine Democrats and Louisiana Democrats today?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0010FJT4VWAsVihqg1j-t_Gb9QtIAgb3UNGxl8j7U80S7yGBkiS4qIm0gmNo74OZ6almguANLL4E4WwZJyOZk_cfPdQpZDY6gmdLwUudGn5iQdzQLZj_2WhcY-JqtMf4iGeRedbj97-d_TdQSrnKReKHbbxlI5AIWsjjml-bEJbbbWBzNfzMbS_sR9FwrOxONi1PFK3j-znW58MhPTgcUUNPMDIgxQFmroBVpWaYHX682rvDng8wgBWTQ==&c=hhEYYuOo6oYCrDRnaEhbiLGXdwWFOeRTbU7gDvhKWHBSfUwRvUI-Pw==&ch=9wWSqIxftMqmsjrOiqKjJBCCzpFbpbrAOCkezoy5ytPb9Q26e3ZSCQ==)
---

In this email, I'm going to ask you to help me get ready for 2028 by becoming a paid subscriber. I'm not being coy about my plans - this isn't a campaign announcement. If you've been reading my posts, you know I've been in the fight for 2026, and I'll keep doing that.
This Substack is reader-supported. Consider becoming a paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..YFIafE_TltTRaAx0BAaDCV0B58X0ZOhnjnqbwD-Th-Q?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=207588786)
As important as 2026 is, though, major questions are waiting for us on the other side of the mid-terms. Voters want to hear new and compelling ideas that have nothing to do with Trump, and they will finally get to have that conversation in a presidential campaign for the first time in 16 years. So what are we offering?
Pennsylvania will be the proving ground for any answer to that question. We hold the key to the White House, and Fetterman's seat may decide control of the Senate. Our (Republican) Attorney General will be up for reelection in 2028, and whether he has the courage to stand up for us against Trump's meddling -- even while he courts Trump's voters -- may be the biggest question no one is talking about yet.
With your help, this Substack can become a meaningful place to prepare for 2028. I've never charged for my posts before, but I'm going to start offering paid subscriptions in addition to the free posts (_**see the link at the bottom to sign up for paid**_). Here's why:
* If I were preparing for the trial of my life as a prosecutor, I'd gather every piece of evidence imaginable. The "evidence" we need for 2028 consists of things like polls, on-the-ground interviews, and conversations with experts, to name a few.
* High-quality video production and strategic advice can turn that evidence into a political argument that breaks through. With your help, I can put this together and share it with you.
* Others do similar work, but very few are on the ground, in a pivotal state, sustaining a conversation directly with voters. This is a unique mission.
* One concrete example: When people tell me Democrats need something new, I tell them about my idea to build government-owned power plants (mostly nuclear) and then force the AI companies to buy power from them. We'd create good-paying jobs, bring down energy prices, reduce our carbon output, and on top of all that, the American people would gain leverage against the most powerful corporations in history. (We could always shut off their power.) People react well in person, but I'd love to study and test this idea more systematically.

A final thought: I had an office in my first congressional campaign in Washington, PA, directly across from where JFK spoke during the 1962 mid-term campaign. Someone sent me the [audio](https://substack.com/redirect/f8be81f7-9a83-459b-a2b3-a0257dfc1b8e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and it's striking how passionate the crowd was. Just a couple of generations later, Trump won that district by 20 points, and those same people told me the Democratic Party had left them. But many still voted for me. Why?
We went everywhere, talked to everyone, and invited everyone in. I saw how important it was to just _listen_. We need to do this on a much larger scale, and I'm asking you to help me figure out how. Become a paid subscriber today. Thanks!

Four others were briefly hospitalized and have since been discharged.

# Sunday, July 19, 2026
---|---
**Good Morning!** On this day in 1879, the notorious gunslinger and dentist [Doc Holliday killed a man](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFugzAURb_GbEa2YzAMHrqwpWtH5OBHeOkDR_ZLEH9fUfUPOp-rq3vP13W8BiTc7p9hBc9zGjfYCwEz5PFVOKf0LN9IBLEkShE33O5hNMq0Ujmp-zEGpGO0VfQzgIFLBV67ztqmcaatFt-F3jrbmhDVfLMzuBigU6D7qMMEqqnQn23K6V4r1dm2blpz06DVNDk9WdUKqyAip1w_Em68wExHekOup7RW5BfmZxGXD2EGYYZ93-sFC6d8nFyYgRcsMoZD4ib_iDDD40WH1L0wQ0yTXBIRnpnzapFzypIXkDPmwpJxhSr7-NyRCEvrhFX3NSD9DuB_WXt78xMAAP__SRWDdw) for the first time after the man shot up his saloon in New Mexico. This marked one of his only eight confirmed shootouts, despite his formidable reputation. If you watched _Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom_ on Sunday evenings in the 1960s, you experienced the very beginning of television's wildlife and nature genre. The brand continues today with both spinoffs and original episodes, as we see in today's [_Whatever Happened To ..._](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQnWNsGDx0QRmarpW6IMAHXHvBEXaCePsqfYXOv_QN_-e1u_YsvM4f_Y18nmK30p6Ecqate6S8xXhPPyxCIUWJgVde577ToO0J3AmbLvQsR2eK4CciTeeCPLramKpy2haL7wHJDgbpPAxTgAqRJsCmNk1NFRIW7F8aOGwQoDa2rKwekBDG0eFowCoDFDjHrfyOvOaFJjnik7ZyjLdC_JLzPanzm9Kt0u2-7-URH_kx0Ksr3aYlbjkp3V7my8zy_jW5VGw-3HcW4WSdMjDfepY_L_9rwtPr3wAAAP__O9Fw7A) section. In case you missed it, this week on _The Flyover Podcast_ , Ayla tackled the phone battery problem that has almost nothing to do with your actual battery. It turns out a handful of settings are running in the background all day, quietly draining power without you ever touching them, and shutting them off costs you nothing. From the toggles most people never think to check to the ones switched on the day the phone left the box, Ayla walked through seven quick fixes that can stretch a single charge well past what you are getting now. [See tips here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykzz1OwzAUAODTOFuj5_9k8ICEspWRslmp_dw8cOMqdltyewRX4AKf9J2O_jhTpvXyNl_RtVT8is-asTXc_L22rZRb_aKcMdaSS6SV1svsBQhzAHvgo48z5d2rLrqEKFB26LgdlNLaCtMtTiVMo0lmECGIGIIelR4HJS2PAGfkHblfDSwfOcCgTK-NOHPkEILlQYFhCjBSK1v_WWhtC6a8lwdufSjXLrultVtl8oWJiYlpL_d278_IxLS8nx7f-oMfF2Byaky-Sim7zcXbk3KmaixTcLnOlP-k9q_-w4mfAAAA___xp2z5)! Today's sponsor is [Frontieras](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO3SAQQL8Gd9fiZTAFRaTV7TZtSoRhbE-CwQJ8V_v3kTdRfiDtnKOZ0fnx7t49Jszbd3-A7WtxGT5agt6huqv1WsrZfmFKEFtJJWLGvHnHKVcPqh_MuOgxfTo5RLsCcBADWKZnKadJczXs1tBJa7MsZpr5ErxYQIuwesEnDsasYkB7b6OaGUbpLNU4Kb4wYDQEzYKkikgKEXup48-Cue-wps_ygjqGcgzJ7r2fjYhvhD8Jf2J-QevjWkvuCNW327qReF79cK1cNQARb3B4TISre3hAxOsg4u30GB-nrz1DbTuef3nwx-lxy1_GP8hm-hCTcH8yXBm7d5KamVOplWZDtfH8wJSwKU0k3e6DXy_3_-r8svx3AAAA__8bjpJR), giving investors the chance to back an emerging energy company developing technology to unlock valuable resources from coal without burning it.

## Two US Soldiers Killed, One Missing
Two U.S. service members [were killed in Jordan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuhDAURL8GOiPbvEzhIg3dpk2JjH2Bu_Fj5etdtH8fkXxC2hlpNOd83ZabQY9x_zQBdNnSEuEkD6VAXp5UckoP-kbvwVHyyWHEuJtFcjkwPjIxLc6gfy9d7fQGIKGtQYtRdV3fj3KoDy16xd0ohdpavgJfwU7tZLixk12nDVSN-lrjo5gE56obmn6QqwDBrR2F7fhQdRwclpSbe8JYDtj8O70gNzaF2uujlAdV7Ucl50rO53k2cbUXxdVfScreVXIO6JwHBoZKJedyJvYkRpBfaIEFCCtkYn-o7J6yM5GZmMoBmQUkwrgzC7GkwMi8iWUbTa-UUKLO2j1O9B5pGKuO78Gg_z1X_mX0peVPAAAA__87X42m) on Friday while defending against Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks, and a third remains missing, U.S. Central Command announced Saturday. Four others were briefly hospitalized and have since been discharged. The strikes follow [a broader wave](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAURp8Gb1hA8N_A0MVbuna0sLnYt8FgwXWs9Omr9BU6f9Knc87XfbpbDBjXT7uDIZ-mCFcJQAR5OgvllI7ywBDAlRSSw4hxtZMSquWi43KYnMXwmnTljAdQcKvAyK7Xumk61VabEfPsZiUHOTRNN4jWq8U3DVin-2GQoq_QvN9EJwcpRK_bumnVLEGKZenkokXLtACHlHL9nTDSBj680hNyvaS9CmYjOgq7fTA1MjVe11Uvc3lbvHemxoBP4OfhLEFhasRsI79s5pTP_eCFskXiyfMt5f384ZbILo_CD8gFbeTrGTxTY5WNOy4MAUvbMS3W3WL4I6B_ZXsa9RsAAP__RF6DoA) of Iranian attacks targeting U.S. allies Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain in recent days. Iran's supreme leader warned of ["unforgettable lessons"](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF6ZwQu8gmKjiO5FkVKkRAaPdycZPMg2oP37iPzCq490dc_5_Tl9OmKKzx9uxaEEmSKembEUTNOeSxLZ8l9iRp-FxVOk-HQTGGi16XT9MXlH_J5s5YeACNhUONRdb-393kFbvQaLLfTB9rObDVgXPBgMs-0NNFjPTVvRcK2Zrv6ojelte7u3MNdYm2Xp6sWaVlmDnoqk2x-hWF4Y-C0Hptsia8XDq5Qtq-ahYFQwnud5W3O8mIIRo96zgvGSuqAk9gpGSi7qvG8JV9SMzmPSbln2jFmXtK-blqAPEnaF4lN7dKwPObMOkhYMO-uEeZOYUcHokn48oJ_Hn0U1oyzkVfP925UUz_wL01alwW8nMVNuO2XNc3XE_8-XLxU_BvgXAAD__9FmmCA) if American strikes continue, and Tehran suspended its commitments to the interim deal signed last month to end the fighting.
## Trump Threatens Tariffs over Smoke

**Whatever happened to _Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom_?** For millions of Americans, Sunday nights meant a folksy zoologist in a khaki shirt saying, _"Welcome to Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom."_ [Here's one of the show's openings](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwVssvgz2wBCpStUhWTsiDJf4tgRcQ2Ll7av0FbqeI_2G_-fZnh0mzNeLu4FpsdgMe03QGmz2XttWylq_MSUItaQSMGO-OsspVweqD2yywWF6WtkFEwE4iA4M06OUw6C56hajwyhjEKMfZhe4F4OLkU18ckpKxoB1aF4a1WxilI5S9YPiMwNGvdfMS6qIpBCwla3_KpjbAjE9ywO23pdbl8zS2lqJOBJ-Ivy073v_LPd2n-H1vxbX_ELE6UHE2_vlOB9Xesk_H91mwrpjSliVJpJebw7TH9n-1eFh-G8AAAD__2qtcVY). The show didn't just fill an hour before the workweek--it invented an entire genre, hauling anacondas and lions into living rooms decades before _Animal Planet_ or _Shark Week_ existed. So where did it go? It never really left. _Wild Kingdom_ debuted on NBC on January 6, 1963, hosted by Marlin Perkins--a University of Missouri zoology dropout. At its peak, the show drew an average of 34 million viewers, powered by [Perkins' scholarly manner and the derring-do of his younger sidekick, Jim Fowler](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQnWNsGDx0QRmarpW6IMAHXHvBEXaCePsqfYXOv_QN_-e1u_YsvM4f_Y18nmK30p6Ecqate6S8xXhPPyxCIUWJgVde577ToO0J3AmbLvQsR2eK4CciTeeCPLramKpy2haL7wHJDgbpPAxTgAqRJsCmNk1NFRIW7F8aOGwQoDa2rKwekBDG0eFowCoDFDjHrfyOvOaFJjnik7ZyjLdC_JLzPanzm9Kt0u2-7-URH_kx0Ksr3aYlbjkp3V7my8zy_jW5VGw-3HcW4WSdMjDfepY_L_9rwtPr3wAAAP__O9Fw7A), who tended to do the actual snake-wrestling while Marlin narrated from a safe distance. This fueled a running gag Johnny Carson loved during their many _Tonight Show_ visits, which became a highlight on Carson's show. [Here's a clip with Fowler, Carson, and a coyote from 1969.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAUheGnwVusC8bgDAyVqrRLMlSqqkwIw3V8E2Iig2Pl7Sv3FbqeI33D_3O0R0eRpsvJ3dGUIdkJ1xyxFJztksuc0iPfKEYMOcUUaKLp4qwAoXagd3xvg6P4srIKZkAU2FRouO6kbFstVDWaHhvetwrbxg8QvIZ2LzoVpO6UGKCDisymgeZ7DtBJVbdK9Bw5eK-5l6CYBAxU0lxfE01lxCG-0hPn2qd7Fc1YyiOz5o2JAxOHdV3rV1rK0uP2b4srfmTN4cma9-PXefk-fVzPn7dqNuGxUoyUlWYSLndH8Y8s_-rwNOI3AAD__woEcQo) But Perkins came by his caution honestly. Back in 1928, as a young reptile curator at the St. Louis Zoo, he was bitten on the finger by a Gaboon viper--one of Africa's deadliest snakes--with no antivenom on hand. He survived, becoming one of only a handful of people ever known to do so. The show ran new episodes from 1963 to 1971, then continued in syndication. In 1985, Perkins stepped down as host to fight lymph cancer; he died at home in St. Louis in June 1986 at age 81. The brand proved durable. _Animal Planet_ revived it in 2002 with Alec Baldwin narrating, and a newer incarnation, _Protecting the Wild_ , is co-hosted by Peter Gros and Dr. Rae Wynn-Grant. Classic Perkins-era episodes [still air Sunday mornings on the nostalgia-oriented MeTV](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGnMVvQ-TA2DB4qtdnSNd2QsY9wrcERdoLy9hV9ha7fJ_2G__UyXBxHXm-fbiFbpjSstOdIpdA2PHLZUrrnH46RQk4xBV55vbkBAfUJzEn2Q3AcX4Oqgp2IkJqKrDSdUm1rUFezbcYOwjS2jiRKEyD0gKgN9k7rrpe6YntoYGQvATql61bjKEmC90Z6BVoooMAlbfV34rXMNMVXetJW-7RU0c6l3LNo3gSeBZ73fa9f6VEeIx3_sbjiZ9Gcn6J59_qrX7K7GvVRbTbcd46RszZCwW1xHP_I8q8OT4u_AQAA__-5YHB5), serving many of the same viewers who grew up on the show. _Were you a fan of Wild Kingdom? For millions of Americans, Sunday nights meant a folksy zoologist in a khaki shirt saying, "Welcome to Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom." . The show didn't just fill an hour before the workweek--it invented an entire genre, hauling anacondas and lions into living rooms decades before Animal Planet or Shark Week existed. So where did it go? It never really left. Wild Kingdom debuted on NBC on January 6, 1963, hosted by Marlin Perkins--a University of Missouri zoology dropout. At its peak, the show drew an average of 34 million viewers, powered by , who tended to do the actual snake-wrestling while Marlin narrated from a safe distance. This fueled a running gag Johnny Carson loved during their many Tonight Show visits, which became a highlight on Carson's show. But Perkins came by his caution honestly. Back in 1928, as a young reptile curator at the St. Louis Zoo, he was bitten on the finger by a Gaboon viper--one of Africa's deadliest snakes--with no antivenom on hand. He survived, becoming one of only a handful of people ever known to do so. The show ran new episodes from 1963 to 1971, then continued in syndication. In 1985, Perkins stepped down as host to fight lymph cancer; he died at home in St. Louis in June 1986 at age 81. The brand proved durable. Animal Planet revived it in 2002 with Alec Baldwin narrating, and a newer incarnation, Protecting the Wild , is co-hosted by Peter Gros and Dr. Rae Wynn-Grant. The declaration would unlock federal money to rebuild homes and infrastructure. [State crews rescued more than 270 people](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ywyAQhU-DOjSwwkYUFGnUOW1KDRKLRIKMB9aWffuMnCOkfm--9_N1GS8upnhdPt2Glp4hj1fca0IiLKObpkxUEX8qlft2c9EfKs4jCDhzobk0o3cxvUbVeDsJb2SDVupeqVNvlG5Wq32nTNC6dxBOJ4OTgj7MSneTAAWITbQHTGhppBQAqu1mCK7THoVxPUjJlEAfKZeWViR8uhrSKz-wtHPemmRXoltl3QeDgcGw73sb8hPOa75XytfDxGA4ejMYNvedC_exukpYuMc5uYKev7E8pJx95UvBhf9tb4r1tz2mFOtZMyWWzcX0zqX_vfWw8BsAAP__YZ-BGg), and local teams near Uvalde about 300 more. ### Come have dinner with us!
|
---|---|---
Supper clubs are a Wisconsin tradition, and Wildflower Supper Club is a part of it! The owners and I are long-time friends and we wanted YOU to join me and Renee for some good food and conversation. Kewaunee. Tuesday. Wildflower Supper Club. 6pm. Can you make it? If you can, Renee and I are so excited to meet you! She’s running for the Assembly’s 1st District, and she’s great company —and exactly the kind of fighter we need in Madison. If not, I’m sure I’ll see you soon! I’m traveling all over Wisconsin talking with folks like you about how we can move Wisconsin forward. Everyone seems to be hopping on the “affordability” bandwagon, but our campaign isn’t about buzzwords. We want REAL change. That means making the rich help fund our public services instead of giving them another tax break. That means fighting for a $22 minimum wage because $15/hour doesn’t cut it anymore. I know we’re all tired of seeing workers lose, and with your help, I can give us a fighting chance. Thanks for being on Team Kat. Katrina deVille Candidate for United States House of Representatives Wisconsin District 8

Experts are saying that there’s just no path back to a Democratic Senate without flipping North Carolina’s crucial seat blue – _something we haven’t done since 2008._
Yet, our progress in this race is undeniable. The momentum is on our side, and that’s causing Republicans to panic. Their dark-money super PACs are spending nearly $100 million to defeat Roy so far, and that surge of cash is having a huge impact.
**Part of my job as campaign manager is deciding where and how much we invest – and, on bad days, where we have to pull back. So I can tell you, when you chip in $5 today, every single penny will help us:**
📺 Launch more TV and digital ads
☎️ Host phone banks and reach voters individually
🚪 Knock on doors to have one-on-one conversations with folks
🚧 Open up more field offices across the state

Simply put, your $5 donation will be put to work immediately to help us win.

name: Jace Yarbrough
subject: Jesus Christ fell three times carrying the Cross
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Yarbrough for Congress
body:
This fight is heavy, and Jesus Christ is my inspiration.

| Friend,
[Jesus Christ carried the cross to Calvary and fell under its weight three times. He stumbled. He rose. He kept walking, because what waited on that hill was salvation for his children.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
I think about that often. This fight for America is heavy too, and Jesus Christ is my inspiration.
I am a husband and a father to five children, and every waking moment I feel the weight of what we're up against.
[An evil communist-minded movement with no fear of God, working to strip away our freedom to worship, to speak, to raise our own kids by our own conscience.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._sviTFr_ek0Wkhxo0yjK5Q)
[Some days I stumble.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.) I wonder if it's worth the cost.
But Jesus Christ didn't reach the throne by ducking the burden.
[He bore the flogging and mockery and shouldered the cross to his eventual death.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._9D4MlnWO4nEc_A)
---
[](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
---
That message fuels me when it would be easier to stay quiet.
History won't hand us a second run at this.
That's why I'm asking you to help me carry this weight and rise to the challenge ahead.
[Whatever you can give, $25, $50, $100, is your hand under this cross with mine. ](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
Even under the heaviest load, we do not stumble alone, because Jesus Christ carried it first, and He carries it with us still.
Let's do this together.

[Chip in before midnight!](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)
May God bless you and your family,
Jace Yarbrough
---

name: Chris Pappas
subject: The price of a scoop 🍦
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Long before I served in Congress, I was in the kitchen at my family’s restaurant in Manchester making homemade ice cream.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7819%2E582294%2E64n7iC)
Happy National Ice Cream Day! 🍦
This is a holiday I can get behind.
Long before I served in Congress – or even thought about running for office – I was in the kitchen at my family’s restaurant in Manchester making homemade ice cream. _Every year we’d churn out more than 35,000 gallons of it!_
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260719_1.N9LEo2&refcode=em20260719-1&t=2&akid=7819%2E582294%2E64n7iC)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260719_1.N9LEo2&amount=5&refcode=em20260719-1&t=3&akid=7819%2E582294%2E64n7iC)**
After scooping that much ice cream, you learn a thing or two about what makes a great flavor. **Fun fact: I even helped create one of the restaurant’s most unique flavors – _Baklava._**
My time spent there taught me the importance of hard work, showing up for your neighbors, and giving back to the community that gave my family so much.
Those values have guided me every day in Congress – and I’ll continue fighting for hardworking Granite Staters in the Senate.
**[So today, if you’re enjoying a scoop of your own, will you chip in $5 or the price of a scoop and help us keep New Hampshire blue?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260719_1.N9LEo2&refcode=em20260719-1&t=4&akid=7819%2E582294%2E64n7iC)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260719_1.N9LEo2&amount=5&refcode=em20260719-1&t=23&akid=7819%2E582294%2E64n7iC)**
Thanks for being part of this team – and happy National Ice Cream Day!
Chris

Peter,

A Los Angeles mayoral candidate, Nithya Raman, recently proposed banning backyard barbecues.

No, this is not satire.

A candidate for mayor of America's second-largest city looked at her constituents cooking dinner in their own backyards and saw a problem that needed a government solution.

This is what Ayn Rand described decades ago.

She wrote, _" We are fast approaching the stage of ultimate inversion: the stage where the government is free to do anything it pleases, while the citizens may act only by permission."_

While she was not talking about barbecues, Ayn Rand was talking about the mindset that eventually gets around to barbecues, because **once the state believes it owns your judgment** -- and your property -- your grill is just the next line item.

Peter, this is exactly the kind of small, absurd, telling moment that shows young people what collectivism actually looks like when it runs out of bigger things to control.

I'm Jennifer Anju Grossman, CEO of The Atlas Society, the largest organization in the world dedicated to bringing Ayn Rand's ideas to a new generation. We create graphic novels, animated videos, a hit podcast, and a growing slate of educational programs, all designed to meet young people exactly where they already are, on the platforms they already use, in formats built to actually hold their attention.

[****](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135563825/634649962/1362877128?refcode=em-7.19.26-all-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNWNhOGIwMS03ZDgzLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Uvr4IT5O5ijA-SBPezvK9T695naw6bZEp1GS-9CEAq0=)_My dad and I!_ That meant being able to buy a home. body:
November feels far away. It isn't. The summer is everything. |
Fellow American,

Every election cycle, there's a window.

It opens in July. It closes in September. And what happens inside that window -- the organizing, the verifying, the quiet work that never makes the news -- is almost always what decides who wins in November.

_The summer is where Senate**majorities** are saved or lost._

Not October when the ads are running and the rallies are packed. Not the final sprint when everyone suddenly pays attention. Right now -- while the beaches are full and the news cycle is loud and most people have their eyes anywhere but Washington.

**[Chuck Schumer has had his eyes on November since the moment the 2024 results came in.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=c881e8ade50e413c8ee93e9081514d2f&_e=YMPFUtYpF3FIXSn5SvTCQPN9dn5p06x0QWjXFe9Y4EqNbtTuc0JZanH9GWlN3yhzb8VXf_CVVcfVIsRKBpvF-IC0JwQkgcUdwL37jethmAD0pctRcgB1GHaQ3VHoYLmUlXA8U8wLlfUgfFwZNS2FNWiOKc1bAMIqH62vWFj1XoMC2_0FETKsMRHjm4DjMRVChBrZACLOyMJqY-nrCYeq5p5MfsrBHWeTf3VT_lTI4p1bpUtmlmqpM1ytlmocgVJ-f7FLzVNQ8eXn21V0gCMQfhJKdGCoRvpCGaMUqD1zGCsqlHTzVeUHS6mBY-tBPZNCa9uVH6kvoWeNtEIHwOBsVwwj9BdOjRtPB8791kPy3aNZ6XF9tCWneGdiD8i03qCy0CYe_xhJRHDSnwjJXsDQiLJPY-M8GuA2HNQYdBeBB-29uOVw1YQ2P37vTALou2FTMQSwzuDop2T8yvGsc4__1DIgLzTBPALajc3HGuVgEJtO0-6dOBGrsREP6FUZIHHzM8oE4_3Pi2g1mmH_dXvHH3UEVgKcbHGY_gMnLZQOwhwmhNzl2Sz3bwsKCfgFdDV4V6wpwJTUqzVu6E4AAc3zcNst-MYJttVV2ZKnnLwgIGbQ1x_mJFnCPDZWj375fZYmJZCPgbdfTZoyydoycuilCwQIobPhfHplFYxbjQ5Cu0BhR20IwNS7B1YH_zw3GUW11Hr75pOh6dTE53QAlvLZ9FeTxzi74joNjUEti8Xkkr8Eruk-O2DFlqNtBkuAl0bWgLeS30QDAFZCqKHsqigdff7hBuSBFsLw4IGgQlqyCeTCRGEZ8XLSDG48UVKAYizxboDIHQlfsojH31kFVaOBJWSnFvag38pH54SA7onEzVA%3D)**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3c9ee5ba-ba09-44f6-8b8e-d1646d1e12f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The World Cup final is later today (Argentina and the legendary Messi versus Spain and Lamine Yamal) at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey--and I'll be watching. My son is an avid soccer fan and watching the games together has been one of those family moments you don't plan but never forget. Sitting on the couch, cheering for the home team (or the favorite...or the underdog...), groaning at bad calls, high-fiving after goals, with the most important people in my world. And of course, how could we not fall in love with the Norwegian viking row?
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cb130c65-fde7-41a9-b35a-a334b19f20df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As I watched the games this year, I was reminded of Franklin Foer's book _[How Soccer Explains the World](https://substack.com/redirect/a4f00d81-ffdb-4746-b6b7-e4df9bb12da9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , which came out in 2004 and used soccer as a lens to explain tribalism, nationalism, corruption, and the enduring power of identity. It was a contrarian book during an era when Thomas Friedman's _[The World Is Flat](https://substack.com/redirect/23f83f5a-d883-4959-8c04-f0a1bbfa418e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ (2005) was on everyone's mind, when globalization was supposed to sand down every rough edge and turn the world into one big market. Who could forget his famous thesis that no two countries that had a McDonald's had ever gone to war with each other?
Foer pushed back. His argument was that the Beautiful Game revealed something uglier underneath. Foer suggested that tribalism doesn't dissolve with free trade but rather deepens. Familiarity breeds contempt, as the old saying goes.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/01d0e382-4393-4f1f-b53e-0edb1d8c9a00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It was easy to see Foer's thesis play out over the past few weeks. Before the tournament even started, there were [boycott calls](https://substack.com/redirect/9b5a62a7-8b2d-4698-aa42-a5f572e88aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from European politicians furious over Trump's immigration crackdowns, his threats against Greenland, and the invasion of Venezuela. Fans from [39 countries](https://substack.com/redirect/0fa6982c-ae58-4d12-99c7-0f1d72351b67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) faced travel bans. A Somali referee who had been selected by FIFA to officiate was refused entry to the United States entirely. Then came the matches themselves: [England versus Argentina](https://substack.com/redirect/220a4d30-89d0-41ce-b326-49858c8e068d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the semifinals--replaying the Falklands War on a pitch in Atlanta, 44 years later, with Argentine fans carrying Malvinas flags into the stadium. And now the final: [Spain versus Argentina](https://substack.com/redirect/285dcada-6578-4b93-96b0-062bb727f509?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which the internet has already dubbed "colonizer versus colonized." Tribalism sure seems alive and well.
And then there's the fact that America doesn't care about soccer nearly as much as other countries. The United States is devoted to football--uniquely American, not really played anywhere else--which is itself an extension of an innate and enduring isolationism, born out of being surrounded by two oceans and friendly countries. We play our own game, on our own terms, declare ourselves the world champion, and the rest of the world can watch or not. Pundits [warned of empty stadiums](https://substack.com/redirect/0fa6982c-ae58-4d12-99c7-0f1d72351b67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), dampened turnout, an American public too indifferent and too polarized to care.
### And then the games started. And none of that happened.
[Attendance shattered the all-time record](https://substack.com/redirect/6c9dc24e-2373-4c4e-9b8a-9f18784eb631?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by June 25...with 48 matches still to play. [Fifty million Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/8eb13bd5-b2fa-4da9-bc5e-c43510788153?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) watched the US lose to Belgium 4-1, and then _kept watching anyway_ , with viewership up [92% over 2022](https://substack.com/redirect/1abc6969-4303-45e1-be2b-5ce45fadfd86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The boycotts fizzled. And the internet flooded with [videos of foreign tourists](https://substack.com/redirect/9debc3e2-7e25-4f3f-a8c6-e8157be8244b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) marveling over our country over Buc-ee's ("A gas station mixed with Disney World wrapped in a gift shop"), over free refills, and bottomless appetizers ("The supply chains of this nation are beyond anything my ancestors imagined") over Texas steaks. The world marveled at the sheer size of everything. _**And ranch dressing**_. Europeans became so enamored with the dressing that the [TSA had to issue a warning](https://substack.com/redirect/2bef3aa4-1bb5-4e40-b6c6-21c4656fc9b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to stop European tourists from packing bottles of ranch dressing in their carry-ons. [Kraft launched a TSA-compliant ranch travel kit](https://substack.com/redirect/986103b5-1a07-452f-ad3b-adcc8a6ccd18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I am not making this up.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cbdecb5f-8d3e-476b-b468-6d0b45a54b2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
As an American [posted on X](https://substack.com/redirect/9debc3e2-7e25-4f3f-a8c6-e8157be8244b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "If you want to hate America, watch the news. If you want to love America, drive across it."
And then there were the moments that made you forget about jerseys and borders entirely. Entire stadiums singing [John Denver's "Country Roads"](https://substack.com/redirect/a020cd26-436d-4f28-b10a-4168c8245589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after every US match...players and fans together, 70,000 voices, arms around strangers. [Japanese fans staying behind to clean the stadiums](https://substack.com/redirect/6bf16279-778d-4ee3-946f-a056b6874172?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after every game, win or lose. A [Spain fan and a Cabo Verde fan swapping jerseys](https://substack.com/redirect/a165f6bd-fc5c-479f-a9c7-5f5e6e2e0a5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the stands with the Cabo Verdean so moved that someone wanted to wear his tiny country's shirt that both men were in tears. [Japanese tourists in cowboy hats](https://substack.com/redirect/3bd2b126-f800-4f34-b079-429417459566?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Houston. A [Mexican fan handing a young English boy](https://substack.com/redirect/6bf16279-778d-4ee3-946f-a056b6874172?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his Merlin the Duck plush after their teams had just played each other.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a4afdd4b-daaa-41b3-bfa3-40691508e787?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Sure, Argentina and England still hold their grudge and Argentina and Spain will relitigate 300 years of colonial history on Sunday. Fans still sing songs about old wars and the tribalism that Foer wrote about hasn't really disappeared. But it's settled in shootouts, not shooting. The grudges are real, the passions are fierce, and at the final whistle, they swap jerseys, embrace the thrill of victory and agony of defeat as competitors who love the sport, and go home.
So maybe soccer really does explain the world. America is easy to hate from afar but harder to hate up close. Soccer is capable of making boycotts fizzle and getting people to overlook policy disagreements long enough to share a stadium. And all of this happened _here_. America hosting, bringing people together, welcoming the world with open hearts, inspiring them with the country we've built. Still the shining city on a hill and a force for good in the world.
* * *
## [America at 250: Still Shining](https://substack.com/redirect/aed38d5a-6472-4cb1-bbaf-b6fdf8cb11f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Jul 4
[](https://substack.com/redirect/aed38d5a-6472-4cb1-bbaf-b6fdf8cb11f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Inspired by my attendance at a naturalization ceremony in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, two years ago, I have been writing about America each year around Independence Day. Spending the day of America's birth with her newest citizens, it was impossible for me not to think about my own family's immigrant journey, and each year I pause and reflect with gratit...](https://substack.com/redirect/aed38d5a-6472-4cb1-bbaf-b6fdf8cb11f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/aed38d5a-6472-4cb1-bbaf-b6fdf8cb11f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
It may not be our national sport, but we still cheer for the home team regardless of political persuasion. Despite divisions and polarization, in the end, we are still a patriotic people. Fifty million people (Yes, 50,000,000) watched a 4-1 loss, after all. Sure, we're all tribal. But today's tribes are capable of playing a sport fiercely and with passion, but also with joy and hugs, and singing songs after, regardless of jersey color.

**VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI** is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. **He 's currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza**. _LinkedIn_ has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and _Worth_ profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, _**[The Making of a Generalist: An Independent Thinker Finds Unconventional Success in an Uncertain World](https://substack.com/redirect/6ccfe9f8-7c2d-4813-a1b0-ac21a4f1aa5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ , _**[Think for Yourself: Restoring Common Sense in an Age of Experts and Artificial Intelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/9d82ccce-28d7-4d02-99ea-aea679565388?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ and _**[Boombustology: Spotting Financial Bubbles Before They Burst](https://substack.com/redirect/b9b34cf3-e400-433d-b1a7-a564eb83a72e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_. How the World Cup Explains America and the World. | | | Jul 19 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- The World Cup final is later today (Argentina and the legendary Messi versus Spain and Lamine Yamal) at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey--and I'll be watching. My son is an avid soccer fan and watching the games together has been one of those family moments you don't plan but never forget. Sitting on the couch, cheering for the home team (or the favorite...or the underdog...), groaning at bad calls, high-fiving after goals, with the most important people in my world. And of course, how could we not fall in love with the Norwegian viking row? As I watched the games this year, I was reminded of Franklin Foer's book , which came out in 2004 and used soccer as a lens to explain tribalism, nationalism, corruption, and the enduring power of identity. It was a contrarian book during an era when Thomas Friedman's (2005) was on everyone's mind, when globalization was supposed to sand down every rough edge and turn the world into one big market. Who could forget his famous thesis that no two countries that had a McDonald's had ever gone to war with each other? Foer pushed back. His argument was that the Beautiful Game revealed something uglier underneath. Foer suggested that tribalism doesn't dissolve with free trade but rather deepens. Familiarity breeds contempt, as the old saying goes. It was easy to see Foer's thesis play out over the past few weeks. Before the tournament even started, there were from European politicians furious over Trump's immigration crackdowns, his threats against Greenland, and the invasion of Venezuela. Fans from faced travel bans. A Somali referee who had been selected by FIFA to officiate was refused entry to the United States entirely. Then came the matches themselves: in the semifinals--replaying the Falklands War on a pitch in Atlanta, 44 years later, with Argentine fans carrying Malvinas flags into the stadium. And now the final: , which the internet has already dubbed "colonizer versus colonized." Tribalism sure seems alive and well. And then there's the fact that America doesn't care about soccer nearly as much as other countries. The United States is devoted to football--uniquely American, not really played anywhere else--which is itself an extension of an innate and enduring isolationism, born out of being surrounded by two oceans and friendly countries. We play our own game, on our own terms, declare ourselves the world champion, and the rest of the world can watch or not. Pundits , dampened turnout, an American public too indifferent and too polarized to care. And then the games started. And none of that happened. by June 25...with 48 matches still to play. watched the US lose to Belgium 4-1, and then kept watching anyway , with viewership up . The boycotts fizzled. And the internet flooded with marveling over our country over Buc-ee's ("A gas station mixed with Disney World wrapped in a gift shop"), over free refills, and bottomless appetizers ("The supply chains of this nation are beyond anything my ancestors imagined") over Texas steaks. The world marveled at the sheer size of everything. And ranch dressing. Europeans became so enamored with the dressing that the to stop European tourists from packing bottles of ranch dressing in their carry-ons. . I am not making this up. As an American : "If you want to hate America, watch the news. If you want to love America, drive across it." And then there were the moments that made you forget about jerseys and borders entirely. Entire stadiums singing after every US match...players and fans together, 70,000 voices, arms around strangers. after every game, win or lose. A in the stands with the Cabo Verdean so moved that someone wanted to wear his tiny country's shirt that both men were in tears. in Houston. A his Merlin the Duck plush after their teams had just played each other. Sure, Argentina and England still hold their grudge and Argentina and Spain will relitigate 300 years of colonial history on Sunday. Fans still sing songs about old wars and the tribalism that Foer wrote about hasn't really disappeared. But it's settled in shootouts, not shooting. The grudges are real, the passions are fierce, and at the final whistle, they swap jerseys, embrace the thrill of victory and agony of defeat as competitors who love the sport, and go home. So maybe soccer really does explain the world. America is easy to hate from afar but harder to hate up close. Soccer is capable of making boycotts fizzle and getting people to overlook policy disagreements long enough to share a stadium. And all of this happened here. America hosting, bringing people together, welcoming the world with open hearts, inspiring them with the country we've built. Still the shining city on a hill and a force for good in the world. | | | | ---|---|--- | Jul 4 | It may not be our national sport, but we still cheer for the home team regardless of political persuasion. Despite divisions and polarization, in the end, we are still a patriotic people. Fifty million people (Yes, 50,000,000) watched a 4-1 loss, after all. Sure, we're all tribal. But today's tribes are capable of playing a sport fiercely and with passion, but also with joy and hugs, and singing songs after, regardless of jersey color. | | ---|---|--- VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. On January 3rd, 2021, I stood in the House chamber and swore to support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic.

Three days later, the Capitol was attacked, and I had a choice to make:_be a politician, or be a patriot._

**I put our republic first: I served on the January 6th Committee, seeking truth, justice, and accountability for the American people.**

That decision may have cost me my House seat in 2022, after an onslaught of MAGA cash targeted our district. But I’d make the same choice all over again, because I swore an oath—the same oath I swore at 17 when I entered the Naval Academy—to protect the country I love.

**That’s why I’m running for Congress in 2026.**

I’m running to help families get ahead instead of just getting by, to ensure veterans get the support they need, and to defend our Constitution.

**Friends,** With just **107 days until the General Election** , our campaign continues to build momentum. Thank you to everyone who has volunteered, donated, attended an event, or simply shared our message. Your support is making a real difference. Right now, we're focused on two things: **getting the Beck for Congress name out across the 5th District and raising the funds to compete this fall.** You may have noticed our new **4' x 4' campaign signs** going up around the district. More are ready to be installed as fundraising allows, helping us reach thousands of voters every day. We're also partnering with **two innovative companies** using **scientific methods and advanced technology** to help us connect with voters who don't usually hear from Democratic campaigns. We believe these new approaches will help us reach independents and other persuadable voters with our common-sense message. Volunteer activity is ramping up as we approach the August primary. **WisDems is organizing canvasses across the district** , and they can always use more volunteers. If you'd like to help, please contact **Claire Brennan** [claire.brennan@wisdems.org](mailto:claire.brennan@wisdems.org) or join a canvass team in your area. You can also sign-up directly via [Mobilize](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a5ce58bf2bd516dceed4cba&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.mobilize.us%2Fwisdems%2F%3Fend_date%3D2026-07-27T04%253A59%253A59.999Z%26is_virtual_flexible%3Dfalse%26start_date%3D2026-07-19T05%253A00%253A00.000Z&w=65ec894f1812f45661bb4481&c=b_6a5ce2897c998378a7e2de52&l=en-US&s=KCPOWxd2ws6aKzsdcz2IDd3bZ-M%3D). Even though I'm the only Democrat on the primary ballot, **please remember to vote for Andrew Beck in the August primary.** A strong turnout shows momentum and gives us an important benchmark as we head into the general election. Finally, the **Common Threads Coalition** is continuing to work on organizing a debate between Congressman **Scott Fitzgerald** and me early this fall. I hope it comes together because the voters of the 5th District deserve to hear both candidates discuss the issues side by side. Please check our events page for [upcoming events](https://v8k6.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a5ce58bf2bd516dceed4cba&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.beckforcongress.com%2Fevents%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D6a5ce2897c998378a7e2de52%26ss_email_id%3D6a5ce58bf2bd516dceed4cba%26ss_campaign_name%3DBeck%2Bfor%2BCongress%2B-%2BJuly%2BUpdate%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2026-07-19T14%253A56%253A27Z&w=65ec894f1812f45661bb4481&c=b_6a5ce2897c998378a7e2de52&l=en-US&s=sRa3zzwh-v7wvnxKiTG8f6jcwT8%3D). Thank you again for standing with our campaign. Together, we're building a grassroots movement to bring new leadership and real representation to Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District. **Thank you for your support!** **Andy** p.s. body:
I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.

| [](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDcxOV9NVy1FUi4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NjA2MTctMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA3MTlfTVctRVIuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTYwNjE3LTI4OTkifQ/4h-pgjvfiEvWm3U__GYhiA)

Peter,
Do you believe in the power of prayer?
My name’s Troy Downing. When America faced its darkest hour after 9/11, I knew I couldn't just sit on the sidelines. I enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and served eight years in a Combat Search and Rescue squadron, deploying twice to Afghanistan.
On those missions, flying into danger to rescue wounded soldiers, you rely on something much bigger than yourself. Through every deployment and dark night, God’s guiding hand was our shield and protection.
Now, as a Member of Congress working to defend the American Dream and protect our GOP Majority, the battlefield has changed, but the spiritual stakes are just as high. I still rely on God’s unchanging, guiding hand every single day.
[If you believe in God and the power of prayer to guide our leaders and protect our land, I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDcxOV9NVy1FUi4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NjA2MTctMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA3MTlfTVctRVIuMTEwMTE3X3QxOTYwNjE3LTI4OTkifQ/66SmXX2XD78OAIkyY0aceg)

Your faith and your prayers are the greatest support I could ever ask for as we fight to keep our nation strong and free.
God Bless,
Troy Downing
U.S. Representative, Montana's 2nd District

On those missions, flying into danger to rescue wounded soldiers, you rely on something much bigger than yourself. Through every deployment and dark night, God’s guiding hand was our shield and protection. Now, as a Member of Congress working to defend the American Dream and protect our GOP Majority, the battlefield has changed, but the spiritual stakes are just as high. I still rely on God’s unchanging, guiding hand every single day. | Your faith and your prayers are the greatest support I could ever ask for as we fight to keep our nation strong and free. God Bless, Troy Downing U.S. Representative, Montana's 2nd District

These are just a few issues that will be top of mind for me as your next governor. They made the list because I've heard about them from folks like you time and again on the campaign trail:
✔️ Standing up to Trump.
✔️ Affordable housing, healthcare, and communities.
✔️ Investments in our public schools.

**She chose to use her campaign website to signal corporate PACs to throw their weight behind her MAGA Republican opponent** who wants more ICE presence in a community already reeling from their cruelty, and supports advancing Trump’s policies — all in hopes of knocking Mai out of the top two so she wouldn’t have to face her in November.
That’s the kind of leader Doris Matsui is. One who would rather help a MAGA candidate advance to the General than pass the torch to the next generation.
_But it didn’t work._
Not only did Mai advance to the general election in November, _she got more votes than Matsui._
That’s because Mai has real roots in her community. She knows exactly what the voters of her district need right now because she’s lived that reality her entire life — as a working mom, as the daughter of Hmong refugees who grew up on SNAP and Medicaid, and as a Sacramento City Council member who has been showing up for her neighbors long before anyone was paying attention.
That’s why they showed up in force for the rally I held with Mai just before her election!

**But I have to be honest, Mai is still facing an uphill battle. Unlike her opponent, she’s refused every dollar of corporate PAC money in this race. That means she depends on dedicated grassroots supporters like you to sustain her fight.**
Leaders We Deserve exists for this exact reason — to make sure candidates like Mai have the resources they need to win, even when the establishment throws everything it has against them.

Give me your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2364%2E791427%2ExHxPJN)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jul26.gZgURP&refcode=em260719-1-180&t=2&akid=2364%2E791427%2ExHxPJN)

Friend — **I am a refugee.**
That’s not something I shy away from. Being a refugee has made me who I am today.
I fled a brutal civil war in Somalia, which is why I understand that diplomacy and peace must always be sought over death and destruction.
I lived in a refugee camp for years, which is why I can stand tough against the insults, conspiracies, and sham investigations that Trump and Republicans constantly throw my way.
I was given an opportunity for a new start in America, which is why I fight for a commonsense immigration system that allows people to come here safely and legally.
My family and I worked hard to afford to live in our new country, which is why I believe in the dignity of the working class and the need for higher wages, healthcare, housing, and a quality education for all.
In 2024, over 100,000 refugees resettled in America. **Trump has now capped that number at just 7,500 a year as part of his extremist immigration regime.**
As we keep up the fight to abolish ICE, close down Trump’s mass detention camps, and reunite families and communities who have been ripped apart, it’s important to remember that we must also fight to live up to America’s promise, inscribed on the Statue of Liberty:
**_"Give me your tired, your poor,
Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free”_
We shouldn’t let fascists like Trump make us afraid of immigrants; we should welcome them. We shouldn’t see immigrants as a problem to deal with; we should talk about the amazing contributions that refugees and all immigrants add to our great nation.
[**If you’re with me in the fight for a better way forward for America’s immigration system, chip in whatever you can afford to my campaign. I’m proud to be a refugee and eternally grateful for everything America has given me, which is why I’m fighting to give back to my community and better the lives of all Americans, no matter where they were born.**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-jul26.gZgURP&refcode=em260719-1-180&t=3&akid=2364%2E791427%2ExHxPJN)

clean_body: Give me your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free Friend — I am a refugee. That’s not something I shy away from. Being a refugee has made me who I am today. I fled a brutal civil war in Somalia, which is why I understand that diplomacy and peace must always be sought over death and destruction. I lived in a refugee camp for years, which is why I can stand tough against the insults, conspiracies, and sham investigations that Trump and Republicans constantly throw my way. I was given an opportunity for a new start in America, which is why I fight for a commonsense immigration system that allows people to come here safely and legally. My family and I worked hard to afford to live in our new country, which is why I believe in the dignity of the working class and the need for higher wages, healthcare, housing, and a quality education for all. In 2024, over 100,000 refugees resettled in America. Trump has now capped that number at just 7,500 a year as part of his extremist immigration regime. As we keep up the fight to abolish ICE, close down Trump’s mass detention camps, and reunite families and communities who have been ripped apart, it’s important to remember that we must also fight to live up to America’s promise, inscribed on the Statue of Liberty: "Give me your tired, your poor, Your huddled masses yearning to breathe free” We shouldn’t let fascists like Trump make us afraid of immigrants; we should welcome them. We shouldn’t see immigrants as a problem to deal with; we should talk about the amazing contributions that refugees and all immigrants add to our great nation. Team, my friends over at Resist Reclaim Rebuild said I could reach out:
I'm honored to share that I have officially become the Democratic nominee for Congress in NY-21.
I am grateful for everyone who has believed that a dairy farmer from the North Country could build something strong enough to compete in one of the most important races in the country.
When we launched back in December of 2024, I didn't do it because I wanted to be a politician. I did it because I love this community, and I believe the people here deserve someone who knows their struggles, because they've lived them too.
Over the last year, I've traveled this district, met with families, listened to workers, farmers, parents, veterans, and small business owners.
Everywhere I went, I heard the same thing: people are tired of being forgotten.
That's what brought us here.
But this isn't the finish line. It's the beginning of the next chapter.
The eyes of the country are turning toward NY-21. More money will enter this race. More attention will follow. The fight ahead won't be easy.
But I've never been afraid of hard work.
On the farm, you don't stop working because you've finished one job. You get up the next morning and start the next one.
That's exactly what we're going to do.
Will you split a donation of $25—or whatever you can afford— between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor of our General Election campaign right now? Your early support is the fuel we need to build a winning infrastructure, hire organizers, and ensure our message reaches every corner of NY-21. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-blake]

Here's a question worth asking:

**Why is one of the bluest districts in California represented by someone who spent 20 years funding endless war and voted to arm Israel's genocide?**

This isn't a complicated question. It's a moral one — and for over 20 years, Doris Matsui answered it the wrong way. She takes AIPAC money, and time and again voted to send our tax dollars and American weapons to Israel while bombs paid for by our government killed innocent civilians.

Last week, under mounting pressure, Matsui finally voted to cut some of this funding. But we shouldn't have to spend 20 years — and an entire campaign — dragging our own representatives toward the right thing. That's not leadership. And it's a big part of why so many people have lost faith that this party will fight for them.

I'm running to change that. And I don't just talk about it — I've already acted.

In 2024, while Doris Matsui was cashing AIPAC checks in Washington, I was in City Hall passing Sacramento's ceasefire resolution. When it would have been easier to stay quiet, I put my values on the record. That is the difference between us, and it always will be.

In Congress, I will fight to end the military aid that enables these war crimes. I will sign onto the Block the Bombs Act on day one to stop the flow of weapons used to kill civilians. And I will say what should be obvious: every dollar we pour into endless war is a dollar stolen from our schools, our housing, and our healthcare here at home.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter, our
communications director Usamah Andrabi said it best:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260719-1-cb.jGd1-6&refcode=em20260719-38048&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38048%2E1203867%2EkHK6s0 ]Tweet by Usamah Andrabi: If you read this, Wesley Bell has nothing to
actually show for his first term in Congress outside of community project
funding equaling 30% of what Cori Bush was delivering for MO-01. He leaves
out his votes to thank ICE, send Israel billions, and enable Trump’s
crypto corruption.

In a recent tweet, Rep. Wesley Bell compared his and Justice Democrat Cori
Bush’s records in Congress — and his attempt to rewrite history is exactly
what we’ve come to expect from a Do-Nothing Democrat like him.

Bell calls himself a progressive. But his actions tell a different story.

While Bell claimed he was fighting to abolish ICE, he neglected to share
that he voted with 75 other establishment Democrats to express gratitude
for ICE.

While he bragged about bringing resources home to St. Louis, he failed to
mention how he voted against an amendment to cut $3.3 billion in funding
to Israel — choosing the priorities of AIPAC and 99.9% of Republicans over
what his constituents are demanding and a majority of Democrats who voted
for it.

And after all that? The community project funding he points to is a
fraction of what Cori delivered for MO-01.

For four years in Congress, Cori championed Medicare for All, fought for
reproductive justice, introduced legislation to demand a ceasefire in Gaza
and end U.S. military aid to Israel, defended marginalized communities,
and stood up to MAGA authoritarianism — even when it wasn’t easy.

She didn’t have corporate lobbyists or AIPAC writing her checks. She
didn’t sell out. And she never stopped fighting for the people of St.
Louis.

Now, Cori’s running to reclaim her seat from a politician who’s delivered
nothing but empty promises and meaningless talking points.

On August 4th, we have the chance to win this rematch and replace an AIPAC
stooge with a real progressive champion to represent St. Louis again.

Our grassroots movement is winning across the country. But the
establishment, their megadonors, and their stooges aren’t going to hand us
this victory. We have to fight for it.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260719-1-cb.jGd1-6&refcode=em20260719-38048&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=38048%2E1203867%2EkHK6s0 ]If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to stand up to the status
quo, Peter, this is it. Can you
chip in $10 to Justice Democrats and Cori Bush’s campaign
today to help us fight like hell and win the MO-01 primary next month?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260719-1-cb.jGd1-6&refcode=em20260719-38048&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1022&akid=38048%2E1203867%2EkHK6s0 ]Contribute $10

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

name: Raja
subject: They chanted "Death to Krishnamoorthi"
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch . Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.
Will you chip in $10, $20, or $50 to Equal Opportunity Now today to help us elect leaders who won't be intimidated — no matter what they face? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi
Founder | Equal Opportunity Now

Friend,

Welcome back to another edition of Sarah Explains It All. My goal with this series is to pull back the curtain on the complicated infrastructure challenges facing Maryland, cut through the noise, and look at the actual facts of how national trends affect your daily household budget.

Today, we need to talk about a massive, invisible factor currently driving up the cost of your monthly utility bills: the explosive growth of corporate data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure.

You have likely seen the headlines about the global boom in AI and cloud computing. What the headlines rarely mention is the staggering amount of electricity required to keep these massive warehouses of computer servers running 24 hours a day.

Because data centers require an astronomical amount of power, the regional electric grid operator has had to greenlight billions of dollars in rapid upgrades to high-voltage transmission lines to keep up with demand. Under current utility rules, corporate tech giants are not required to cover those upgrade costs themselves. Instead, the costs are spread out and passed down to regular utility customers.

In fact, the Maryland Office of People's Counsel recently filed a formal complaint [https://insideclimatenews.org/news/30062026/ferc-order-data-center-grid-costs/] with federal energy regulators warning that under the current system, Maryland homeowners face paying an extra $1.6 billion on their electric bills to subsidize the power infrastructure needed for these data centers.

Residential energy rates in Maryland have already risen significantly over the last several years. Forcing families who are already watching every dollar to pay even higher monthly bills to foot the tab for multi-billion-dollar tech corporations is flat-out wrong.

That is exactly why I am taking direct action by cosponsoring the Power for the People Act in Congress. This legislation is built on a very simple, fair principle: if a massive corporation wants to build a data center that puts a heavy strain on our local grid, they should have to pay for the infrastructure required to run it, not regular Maryland families.

The Power for the People Act would officially direct federal energy regulators to rewrite the rules, forcing data center operators to pay for local grid upgrades directly. It also creates common-sense consumer protections by incentivizing tech giants to bring their own new, clean energy generation and battery storage systems online alongside their facilities, ensuring they don't trigger local power outages or blackouts during peak summer heat waves.

Public service should always be about protecting consumers and fighting for the economic well-being of the people we represent. There’s more work to be done to rein in data centers, but we have to start by making sure regular citizens aren’t getting squeezed.

If you want to keep a determined advocate fighting to protect your wallet and bring real accountability to our energy grid, consider joining our team for the long haul.

**My background is a little different than some of my colleagues in Congress.**
I grew up in a working-class family, and I’m the granddaughter of a police officer and the daughter of two teachers. As a child, I had an interest in engineering, which led me to receive a college scholarship to study electrical engineering.
I worked at General Motors before transitioning to running a small business with my husband in Oregon. Then, I went on to serve my community in the Oregon State Legislature.
I was proud to fight for Oregonians in Salem and work to ensure our voices were heard. But I knew I had to do more if I was going to build a better future for the next generation.
That’s why I decided to run for Congress in 2024. It was an extremely competitive race, but with the support of this grassroots team, we flipped OR-05 from red-to-blue — and I became Oregon’s first Black U.S. Representative.
I’m honored to be working for the good people of Oregon’s 5th District in Washington and fighting to deliver practical solutions to the issues impacting our communities — from working to lower costs to protecting affordable healthcare to strengthening public education.
**I’m proud of the work I’ve accomplished, and I’m determined to continue fighting for the next generation in Congress — and I’d appreciate your support.**

We need to respond | There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five.

Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, **the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135575083/634680768/-328725030?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.19_Mary-Peltola-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYjBhNGMwZS04ZDgzLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ODHrfJ4x2pIdfWfLak6b4Ka4jucs6_TD5vQrZQKboVY=) We need your help to respond.

**Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up.**

They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map.

They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer.

They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them.

They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – twice – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state.

**They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out.**

Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – _and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition!_

We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves.

**But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war – reaching communities on and off the road system, from the Aleutians to Anchorage to the Arctic.**

No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it. clean_body: We need to respond | There have been six polls in the six months since I launched this campaign for Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat. We were leading in the first five. Then, after my opponent and the billionaires and super PACs that back him started spending millions on attack ads against me, the New York Times/Siena University poll released this month shows us down two points. = We need your help to respond. Election forecasters like Cook Political Report, Sabato’s Crystal Ball, Split Ticket, and VoteHub have all called Alaska’s U.S. Senate race a toss-up. They shifted the race in our favor because they know we can win, and that all eyes are on Alaska this year in what’s shaping up to be the most competitive and consequential race on the Senate map. They know we can win because Alaskans are fed up with the rigged system that’s pricing us out and threatening our way of life while DC politicians and their donors make themselves richer. They know we can win because my opponent, Dan Sullivan, is the least popular senator up for reelection, and Alaskans want someone who will fight for their healthcare, jobs, disaster relief, and public media – not gut them. They know we can win because I’ve won Alaska statewide – twice – against our former governor Sarah Palin, and now we’re building a movement that’s ready to take on the rigged DC system so we can lower costs, save our fisheries, and bring abundance back to our state. They know we can win this toss-up Senate race if we can raise the resources needed to overcome the attack ads and get our message out. Our fight for fish, family, and freedom resonates in every region of our big, beautiful state – and in a state as big as Texas, Montana, and California combined, that’s a pretty broad coalition! We’re criss-crossing as much of Alaska’s 586,000 square miles as we can to bring every village and every voter into our campaign, and we’re doing all we can to fight back with ads online and on the airwaves. But this is without a doubt the most expensive state on the map to run a Senate campaign. To win in Alaska means building a strong ground game and winning the screen war – reaching communities on and off the road system, from the Aleutians to Anchorage to the Arctic. No one ever said flipping Alaska’s Senate seat was going to be easy. But we do know that this is our best chance to do it. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Mary Peltola and Maggie Hassan will go through immediately: | | = | = | = | = | = | = That’s the power of a grassroots movement. We can win this when we all chip in together. = Your support makes a huge difference. I’m humbled to have you with me in this campaign for Alaska’s toss-up Senate seat, and even more so in this fight for fish, family, and freedom. 🐟❤️🇺🇸 Let’s go win. \- Mary | = It's Maggie Hassan — New England sports fan, crossword enthusiast, mom of two, former governor, and proud U.S. Senator representing New Hampshire since 2016. Over 100 Democrats voted this week to end U.S. military aid to Israel by backing Rep. Thomas Massie's amendment to zero out that funding.
